the nonlinear behavior of passive AlGaAs waveguide is highly sensitive to the bandgap energy.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents the most efficient passive nonlinear waveguide for wavelength conversion in the 1550-nm band.

the results presented here demonstrate that the use of bandgap engineering to suppress two-phonon absorption in AlGaAs waveguide devices is a promising route to achieve efficient wavelength conversion.
we have shown that the use of a passive waveguide, where the bandgap of the core material is engineered to be close to the pump wavelength, can lead to efficient wavelength conversion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonlinear figure of merit of the waveguides is 2.4  W−1 cm−2, which is 2.3× and 3.5× larger than those of the state-of-the-art silicon and silicon nitride waveguides, respectively.
we have demonstrated efficient continuous wave (CW) four-wave mixing in a passive waveguide with a bandgap engineered to suppress two-phonon absorption and minimize the linear loss.
we have achieved the highest conversion efficiency in a passive semiconductor waveguide.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nonlinear figure of merit can be increased by orders of magnitude in bandgap-engineering materials, and that the figure of merit of a nonlinear waveguide is a function of the wavelength, pump power, and the nonlinear coefficient of the material.
the nonlinear figure of merit of a waveguide is not a single parameter, but rather a combination of material, waveguide, and pump properties.
the nonlinear figure of merit (NLFOM) is a useful metric to compare the efficiency of nonlinear processes in different waveguides.
